title: AP/Marshall Project: Maine ICE Agent Brouillette Had Documented Violent History; Hired Anyway
excerpt: An Associated Press investigation revealed that David Brouillette, the ICE agent who fatally shot Colombian national Johan Sebastián Durán Guerrero in Maine, had a long, documented history of domestic violence and serious mental health struggles — yet was hired by ICE after only about eight months with the agency.
content:
Following the July 13, 2026 fatal shooting of Johan Sebastián Durán Guerrero in Biddeford, Maine, the Associated Press and The Marshall Project identified the shooter as ICE agent David Brouillette — an Army veteran and former correctional officer whose family members described him as profoundly unstable and dangerous.

The AP found that Brouillette had a long history of verbal and physical abuse documented in Maine's family court system. Two former wives detailed abuse to the AP. One reported that he left a threatening voicemail late in 2025, around the time he was hired by ICE. Despite these documented red flags, he was hired and placed in the field after approximately eight months as an ICE agent.

  • Brouillette had previously held short stints at a Maine prison, the state Health and Human Services Department, and as a VA police officer — each lasting less than a year.
  • Former ICE officials told the Boston Globe that rapid hiring practices may allow applicants to receive "tentative selection letters" and begin work on temporary status before full background checks are completed.
  • Research by the American Psychological Association has found that a history of domestic violence among law enforcement recruits correlates with higher rates of misconduct and use-of-force complaints.
  • ICE confirmed Brouillette had "nearly a decade of federal law enforcement experience" but did not address whether his domestic violence history was reviewed.

Democratic members of Congress stated that Brouillette's background "directly calls into question the supposed vetting and training ICE does of its recruits."
source: Associated Press / The Marshall Project / Boston Globe
